structure: Part 1 read, in full, the 15 files of the shared chrome and the set's mount: src/server/app/shared/layout.njk (130 lines: GOV.UK template with head, pageTitle, header, service navigation, phase banner, back link, notification banners, journey strip, journeyContent block and footer), kit.js (316 lines: shared copy resolution, surfaces, journey strip, error summary and field error builders, exit/change/run navigation targets, base and server-wide view-model chrome, recoverable save, stale-action redirect, page route pair, date reading and date field builder), save-actions.njk (the save-and-continue / save-and-return / cancel controls), section-caption.njk, error-summary.njk, error.njk, set-context.js (219 lines: set mounts, path-to-set resolution, request set context, required seams), paths.js (route shapes and prefixed links), copy.js and copy-leaves.js (locale resolution and the copy-leaf convention), copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (every shared string and validator default, English and machine-draft Welsh), sets/high-risk-plants/set.js (set id and base), journeys/linear/config.js (templates folder, layout, session cookie names) and routes-high-risk-plants.js (113 lines: the set's plugin registration, set-context hooks, journey flow configuration, entry guard and route mount). It covered: the page chrome (title pattern, header, service navigation and its four signed-in items, alpha phase banner, back link, notification banners for recoverable errors and stale actions, journey strip, footer links), the absence of a language toggle and breadcrumbs, the kit's behaviours every page shares (error summary, inline errors, save-and-return to the overview, change-from-check-answers return, opening-run navigation, session auth on every page route, stale-action redirect, recoverable save, date field format), the save actions macro and its rule for which pages show the return controls, the section caption, error summary and error page templates, every shared copy string in English and its Welsh counterpart, the validator default messages, and the set's id, mount, URL shapes, layout, session cookie names, entry guard and boot-time configuration checks. Unit tests (*.test.js) were not read, as the partition excludes them. One lookup outside the read list (src/config/nunjucks/context/context.js, by grep) confirmed where the layout's addressBookUrl, activeNavigationItem and staleActionRejected values come from; claims resting on it are inferred and say so.

claims.statement: A back link reading 'Back' appears above the content only when the page supplies a back link destination.
Page content sits in a two-thirds column by default (the 'form' surface); a page can use the full-width 'display' surface instead.

When a save hits a recoverable backend failure, the page shows a notification banner titled 'There is a problem' with role alert, saying 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'

The recoverable-error banner says the answers on the page have been saved, although the banner is raised because the save to the backend failed. Recorded as an ambiguity: which store holds the answers when the backend save fails is not shown in this part.
A recoverable backend error during a save is handed to the page's own failure handler instead of failing the request; a stale concurrency token or any other error is not treated as recoverable.

When a form is submitted with a stale concurrency token (the notification changed since the page was opened), the user is redirected back to the same page with staleAction=1 added to its query string.

A page reached with the stale-action flag shows a notification banner (role alert) titled 'The notification has been updated' saying 'This notification was updated since you opened it. Review the details and try again.'
Every journey page carries the notification's concurrency token in its view model, so a submit can be checked against the version the user saw.
claims.quote: concurrencyToken: journey?.concurrencyToken ?? null,

claims.statement: There is no language toggle: the layout renders none, and every call site resolves English copy because no locale selection (cookie or toggle) is wired yet. Looked in layout.njk and copy.js.

Every call site resolves `en` because no locale toggle is wired yet — locale
 * selection (cookie, language toggle) plugs in via the `locale` argument.

claims.statement: A copy value must be either a non-blank string or a function that builds a string from parameters; an empty or blank string is not valid copy.
claims.quote:
export const isCopyLeaf = (value) =>
  typeof value === 'function' ||
  (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0)

claims.statement: A page with validation errors shows a GOV.UK error summary titled 'There is a problem', with one entry per field error.
Each error summary entry links to its field on the same page (#field) by default; a page may make entries link somewhere else, such as another page.
claims.quote: errorList: entries.map(([field, text]) => ({ text, href: href(field) }))

claims.statement: The error summary takes focus when it appears, unless the page renders it without the user having just been refused, in which case focus stays where it is.
No error summary is shown when there are no field errors.
A field with an error shows that error's message inline as the field's GOV.UK error message, the same text as its error summary entry.
claims.quote:
export const fieldError = (fieldErrors, field) =>
  fieldErrors?.[field] ? { text: fieldErrors[field] } : undefined

export const exitTarget = (request, fallback) =>
  hubExitTarget(request) ??
  (changeContext(request)
    ? pagePath(request.params.journeyId, CYA_SLUG)

claims.statement: After 'Save and continue', a user in the opening run of a notification goes to the run's next target; otherwise they go to the next page in the current section.

export const nextTarget = async (request, page, scope) =>
  exitTarget(
    request,
    (await runTarget(request, page.id, scope)) ??
      nextInSection(page.id, scope, request.params.journeyId)
  )

claims.statement: The server refuses to start if the plants set has left a required configuration seam unconfigured, naming each missing seam and the call that would configure it.
At start-up the plants set checks that its obligations are pure and that every obligation has a fulfilment binding, and stops the server if not.
claims.quote:
assertObligationPurity()
        assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage()
claims.note: That a failed assertion stops start-up is inferred from the assert naming and its place in plugin registration; the assert bodies are outside this part.

claims.statement: The plants set's request guards are sandboxed to its own routes, so another set mounted on the same server does not run plants' guards.

Which set a request belongs to is read from its URL path against the registered mounts, the longest matching mount prefix winning; /health, /auth/* and unrouted URLs outside every mount belong to no set.
claims.quote:
Longest match wins, so a set mounted at `/high-risk-plants/extra` would beat
 * one at `/high-risk-plants` rather than depending on registration order.

claims.statement: A set must be mounted at a prefix beginning with '/'; the server refuses to register one without it.
